messages.subject: scatterplot with melted data.set?
parts:
Hi!

I have a melted data.set with radiometric measurements such as:

> ref20110401m[1:10,]
spectrum File Target Calib Int.ext Rel.Abs Wavelength Reflectance
1 spectrum00050.ref 50 SW SW Int Abs 325 1.30380034
2 spectrum00051.ref 51 W SW Int Abs 325 1.10489964
3 spectrum00052.ref 52 RN SW Int Abs 325 -0.23644058
4 spectrum00053.ref 53 RG1 SW Int Abs 325 0.05574192
5 spectrum00054.ref 54 RG2 SW Int Abs 325 0.30506665
6 spectrum00055.ref 55 RG3 SW Int Abs 325 -0.05718166
7 spectrum00056.ref 56 NRN SW Int Abs 325 0.14130642
8 spectrum00057.ref 57 NRG1 SW Int Abs 325 0.03673076
9 spectrum00058.ref 58 NRG2 SW Int Abs 325 0.49297717
10 spectrum00059.ref 59 W W Int Abs 325 1.20279181

with which I can plot Reflectance vs. Wavelengths conditioned to other
categorical variables such as
> qplot(x=Wavelength,y=Reflectance,data=ref20110401m,color=Calib,xlim=c(400,800)) + facet_wrap(~Target,nrow=4)

Nevertheless, now I want an scatterplot comparing Reflectance of the
same targets but using different calibration panels (the Calib
variable above).
Is it possible doing this with the same melted dataset?

My solution has been making 2 different data sets, one for each
calibration type:

> subsref20110401m = ref20110401m[(ref20110401m$Target=="SW" | ref20110401m$Target=="W" | ref20110401m$Target=="RN" | ref20110401m$Target=="NRN"), ]
> subsref20110401m = subsref20110401m[subsref20110401m$Int.ext=="Int", ]
> subsref20110401mSW = subset(subsref20110401m, Calib=="SW")
> subsref20110401mW = subset(subsref20110401m, Calib=="W")
and then, for example:
> qplot(x=subsref20110401mW$Reflectance,y=subsref20110401mSW$Reflectance) + facet_wrap(~subsref20110401mW$Target,nrow=2)

But I'm not sure this is a good approach, as it relies too much on
both datasets having the same ordering.
An alternative would be one single dataset with 2 measure variables,
i.e. ReflectanceW and ReflectanceSW, would this be better?
If so, which would be the way of creating the melted dataset with the
2 Reflectance variables?
My melted dataset comes from
> ref20110401m = melt(ref20110401t,id.vars=1:6)

where ref20110401t is such as
> ref20110401t[1:10,1:8]
ref20110401t[, 1] File Target Calib Int.ext Rel.Abs 325 326
13 spectrum00050.ref 50 SW SW Int Abs 1.30380034 0.85354859
14 spectrum00051.ref 51 W SW Int Abs 1.10489964 0.74327749
15 spectrum00052.ref 52 RN SW Int Abs -0.23644058 -0.07332540
16 spectrum00053.ref 53 RG1 SW Int Abs 0.05574192 0.09370402
17 spectrum00054.ref 54 RG2 SW Int Abs 0.30506665 0.18761399
18 spectrum00055.ref 55 RG3 SW Int Abs -0.05718166 0.05700703
19 spectrum00056.ref 56 NRN SW Int Abs 0.14130642 0.04477394
20 spectrum00057.ref 57 NRG1 SW Int Abs 0.03673076 0.11301020
21 spectrum00058.ref 58 NRG2 SW Int Abs 0.49297717 0.18312812
22 spectrum00059.ref 59 W W Int Abs 1.20279181 1.07243621
and
> dim(ref20110401t)
[1] 17 757

Thanks!

Agus

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: scatterplot with melted data.set?
parts:
I see the problem and I'm afraid I don't have a solution. You essentially want to match your data up in columns in the right order when they may not necessarily be in the right order.  All I could come up with is some nasty for loops that go through every row one at a time matching up the filenames and wavelengths. It's ugly and there's probably a better solution. 

I thought maybe cast() could do it, but I couldn't nail it down. 

Maybe someone else will have an idea. Perhaps even R help since it's more of a data manipulation issue.

Brandon
